newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stocks close all-time-high at 75,263.85.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stocks close all-time-high at 75,263.85.

text.p: The Turkish stock market index closed 1.92 percent higher on Thursday to close at an all-time-high of 75,263.85.
Brokers said that continuing cash influx into the market pushed the index up, adding that there was no fundemantal reason behind the rise.
"There is no improvement in the economy in general. But the prices were cheap," said Nalan Erkarakas, assistant to general manager at Kentbank.
The steady T-bill and lira rates were also among other reasons for the rise in stock prices, brokers said.
"Recently the grip of both the Treasury and Central Bank was felt in the markets. This delayed any financial crisis expected to erupt in September," said Erkarakas.
Brokers also blamed technical factors for the index's uptrend.
"The index breached 80-cent level, thus the mid-term direction is up," said Resat Kutucular from Toros securities.
The demand were highly selective and focused on index shares, Kutucual said.

"I think the rally is going to gather further force. With the central bank in control of money, funds could flood into the market," said Atilla Yesilada, director of research at Global Securities in Istanbul.

Yesilada said concerns about domestic debt and fears of a sharp rise in interest rates over the winter have now eased following a successful beginning to the government's programme of issuing foreign-currency denominated debt.
"The benefits of this are now feeding through into shares," he said.
However, some brokers are still uneasy about the future of the upward movement.
"Is it permanent ? It is hard to say that because the problems in the economy have been growing," said Erkarakas.

"The central bank pressure keeps the interest rates at these levels. Otherwise they should rise," said Kutucular. "The September inflation figure which will be disclosed on Friday might affect the market," he added.
Out of the 225 shares traded, 129 went up, 52 declined while 44 remined steady.
Financial index .ISEF rose 3.43 percent to 67,681.79, industrial index ended 1.31 percent up at 82,070.03.
Actives were utility firms Cukurova elektrik rising 5,000 lira to 74,000, Aktas Elektrik, ending 3,000 lira up at 62,000.
Daily trading volume was 24.52 trillion lira, up from 12.16 trillion on Wednesday.
